messages:
Marta López: Quick heads-up — I'm starting a sweep of token-bucket + queue-priority knobs for small VPC slices. Goal: reduce p95 regressions we've been seeing on 4xA10s when traffic bursts hit. :eyes:

Ajay Patel: Nice. Which knobs are you planning to vary? token_budget_target, max_batch_tokens, queue_priority_threshold?

Marta López: Yup — specifically: token_budget_target (0.5/1.0/2.0), max_batch_tokens (512/1024), enqueue_timeout_ms (5/10/20), and a simple priority demotion for long-running requests. Also toggling KV cache soft-eviction (on/off).

Ryan Chen: Can you capture a profile before/after? I want to compare kernel selection changes and memcpy spikes. I saw a weird regression yesterday where kernel fallback to generic matmul spiked at ~30% of tokens.

Marta López: Will do. Plan: run a 30-min soak with the customer prompt set (small-seq/long-seq mix), perf traces, and collect runtime logs + nvprof traces. Repro command: ```./rb-loadtest --target vpc-slice-small --model rw-13b-quant --workload workload_cust_mix.yml --trace perf --out /tmp/sweep/18765```

perf-bot: Automated perf report queued (run 18765). Expected completion ~30m. See /perf/reports/18765 when ready. :robot_face:

Ajay Patel: A couple of asks: 1) Add the kernel-selection debug flag (`RUNTIME_DEBUG_KERNELS=1`) so we can see when we fall back. 2) Record KV cache hit/miss and eviction counts in the trace.

Marta López: Added both. Also going to try a variant that reduces batch formation aggressiveness (lower batching window) to prioritize latency in VPC constrained hosts.

Ryan Chen: FYI — earlier profiling showed most slowdowns were memcpy staging to device when batches had heterogenous sequence lengths. If we reduce max_batch_tokens but allow more small batches it might help, but cost goes up. Keep an eye on token-cost delta.

Sophia Blake: For canary rollout: please use a config override in the Private control plane and pin only one small-slice tenancy. Don't touch global defaults. Also set autoscale to disabled for the slice so we don't confound results.

Marta López: Will create override JSON and attach. Example override (applies to /private/slices/small-4xa10):
```json
{
  "batching": {
    "max_batch_tokens": 512,
    "enqueue_timeout_ms": 10,
    "token_budget_target": 1.0,
    "queue_policy": "priority-demote-long-reqs"
  },
  "kv_cache": { "soft_eviction": true }
}
```

Ajay Patel: That queue_policy looks good for an experiment. Make sure the demotion threshold is explicit (e.g., requests > 800 tokens).

Marta López: Will set demotion_threshold_tokens=800. Also adding a metric to the console: `batch.slices.small.queue.demotions` so we can graph it.

deploy-bot: Canary override created for /private/slices/small-4xa10 by Marta López (id: override-18765). Rolling to 1 node.

perf-bot: Perf report 18765 ready — quick highlights:
- baseline p95=160ms (hosted) -> canary p95=210ms with high token_budget_target
- KV miss rate jumped 2.3x when soft_eviction=false
- memcpy_wall_time increased +42ms at 75th percentile for mixed-length batches
- kernel_fallback_count increased 18% when token_budget_target >=2.0
Full report: /perf/reports/18765.html

Ryan Chen: Interesting — kernel_fallback correlates with larger token_budget_target. Maybe the runtime picks a different fused-kernel when it expects bigger accumulated tokens and hits memory layout it doesn't support well. We should try forcing kernel policy to prefer the small-seq specialized kernel as a test.

Marta López: I spun another run with token_budget_target=0.5 + max_batch_tokens=1024 (lower budget but larger batch token cap) to see the trade-offs. Results: p95 ~ 170ms, memcpy down ~20ms, kernel_fallback back to baseline. Cost tokens per request up ~6%.

Sophia Blake: That's promising. Can we formalize an SLA-friendly default for Private: token_budget_target=0.75, max_batch_tokens=768, enqueue_timeout_ms=10, kv.soft_eviction=true? Then allow customers to opt into high-throughput mode (token_budget_target>=1.5) with clear perf/cost warnings.

Ajay Patel: +1. Also add a runtime flag to force kernel selection per-model as a short-term mitigation for slices with known regressions. We should not make it default though.

Marta López: I'll draft a proposal doc with numbers, configs, and recommended defaults. Plan to push to /docs/private/batching-guides and leave the override in place for another 24h. If perf stays okay we'll roll to other small slices.

Ryan Chen: If you need me to run a microbench to try the forced kernel policies let me know — I can script it against CI slice.

Marta López: Thanks — will ping. tl;dr: sweep done, found kernel fallback correlated with high token_budget_target, KV soft-eviction helps on constrained hosts, and a mid-range default looks like best tradeoff for Private VPC small GPUs. :thumbsup:

Sophia Blake: Great work — keep ops in the loop and notify customers on any changes to Private defaults.

Marta López: Will do. Closing thread once I post the proposal.
